_comment: Mean micro-time, drawn by emtk. The Qt tool's AutoForm spec is micro_time.view.json.

sections.title: Settings
sections.description: The source file, the minimum photon count, the detector window that is shown and the actions that compute and write the maps.
Compute the maps, write them out, explore them or go on to the next step.

buttons.label: Run
buttons.description: Compute the mean micro-time and intensity of every detector window, in the background. Nothing is recomputed when neither the file, the windows nor Min. photons changed.

buttons.label: Add mean micro-time to HDF5
buttons.description: Add the mean micro-time columns to the imaging HDF5 of the pipeline (the file the Intensity step created); when none is remembered a file is asked for. Created if it does not exist.

buttons.label: Save container
buttons.description: Write the same table as a mean_micro_time artifact into the container beside the photon file (the Qt tool did this when it closed).

buttons.label: ndX
buttons.description: Explore the per-pixel table in ndX, the shared live dataset. A Back button returns to the maps.

buttons.label: Next
buttons.description: Remember the file and the HDF5 and go to the next analysis step. Only available inside the Imaging Tools pipeline.

sections.label: TTTR file
sections.placeholder: pick a file, drop one here, or load from the database
sections.description: PTU/HT3 imaging file with line and frame markers (or drop one onto the window: it is loaded and run). Press Enter to select a typed path.
Pick the photon file from disk or from the database.

buttons.label: Browse
buttons.description: Browse for a photon imaging file on disk.

buttons.label: Database
buttons.description: Load a dataset registered in the database; the database resolves it to a local file wherever its object store keeps the data.

sections.label: Min. photons
sections.description: Pixels with fewer photons than this are discriminated (set to 0); press Run to apply.

sections.label: Detector window
sections.description: The detector window shown in the maps. Every window is computed and written; this only chooses which one is displayed. The windows come from the Detectors tab (or the Imaging Tools setup step); without any, the channel-0 window is used.
What was computed: the file, the size of the image and the detector windows.
